title: Friday Sermon 58: Sura 2, Gabriel, Angels, Dawn Prayer, and Divine Correction (1982-11-12)
source_file: data/sources/playlists/audio-transcripts/58 - Friday Sermon 12 Nov 1982 By Dr Rashad Khalifa.csv
document_summary: A Friday gathering continuing Sura 2 from verses 88 through 101. The opening stresses accepting the whole Quran rather than selecting convenient parts. The study treats shielded hearts, resentment toward a messenger chosen by God, the calf, Sinai, exclusive claims to Heaven, Gabriel and Michael, revelation into Muhammad's heart, and repeated covenant violation. A long question-and-answer section concerns Gabriel's function, angels awakening believers for Dawn Prayer by speech, knocks, or pinches, protective guards, and a personal story in which Rashad expected a corrective pinch after praising the smell of an intoxicant and then faced a dangerous furnace-gas incident.

related_duplicate_sources.note: Study 57 ends near the cow narrative and visible miracles.
The 1982 recording focuses on guardian angels and Fajr awakening.

content_guidance.instruction: The angel discussion follows from Gabriel's verses.

content_guidance.rule: Strongly safeguard experiences of voices and touch

content_guidance.instruction: It is a personal interpretation, not a safety rule.

sections.title: Accepting the whole Quran, selective obedience, war, and divided scripture
sections.summary: Rashad says people cannot accept convenient Quranic teachings while refusing difficult ones. Iranian and Iraqi soldiers praying before fighting and other conflicts illustrate following one part while violating another. Sura 15's condemnation of dividing scripture is invoked.
